title: What is the Medicare Levy Surcharge?
text:
Health Insurance
About Private Health Insurance
Medicare Levy Surcharge
What is the Medicare Levy Surcharge?
A surcharge between 1% and 1.5% of your income if you don’t have private hospital cover.
The good news is that you can buy a basic level of hospital cover for around the same price as (or even less than) the additional tax you might have to pay.
Get a quote
The Medicare Levy Surcharge was introduced by the Australian Government to encourage people who earn above a certain income to take out hospital cover, and to use the private system to reduce demand on public hospitals.
How does the Medicare Levy Surcharge work?
If you’re single and earn over $105,000 (or a couple or family earning over $210,000), buying private patient hospital cover may help you to minimise your tax by avoiding having to pay the Medicare Levy Surcharge. Single parents and couples (including de facto couples) are subject to family income threshold.
The Medicare Levy Surcharge is a surcharge of between 1% and 1.5% of your income if you don’t have private hospital cover. The good news is that you can buy a basic level of hospital cover for around the same price as (or even less than) the additional tax you might have to pay.
The Medicare Levy Surcharge is calculated on a daily rate, so if you only have hospital cover for part of the financial year, you may have to pay Medicare Levy Surcharge for the remaining part of the year.
Doesn't everyone pay the Medicare Levy?
There are two parts to the Medicare Levy:
Most of us pay a 2% Medicare Levy as part of our tax to help fund Medicare.
Higher income earners are also charged an additional Medicare Levy Surcharge of 1% to 1.5% if they don’t have hospital cover.
The following table shows the Medicare Levy Surcharge income thresholds and rates as set by the Australian Government, effective from 1 July 2026.
Singles | Couples & Families | Medicare Levy Surcharge Rate
$105,000 or less | $210,000 or less | 0.00%
$105,001 – $123,000 | $210,001 – $246,000 | 1.00%
$123,001 – $164,000 | $246,001 – $328,000 | 1.25%
$164,001 or more | $328,001 or more | 1.50%
These income thresholds apply for the 2026–27 financial year (1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027). For prior financial year thresholds, visit PrivateHealth.gov.au.
Single parents and couples (including de facto couples) are subject to family tiers. If you have dependent children, your income threshold for Medicare Levy Surcharge purposes increases by $1500 for each child after the first. To determine whether your child is a dependent for tax purposes or if you want more information about Medicare Levy Surcharge levels, please contact your registered tax agent or visit the ATO website.
Persons covered as dependents under parent’s policy are not liable to pay the MLS
Where a person earning above the MLS threshold has an appropriate level of hospital cover on their parent’s policy, they are not subject to the MLS. This is the case irrespective of whether they are an adult dependent or a dependent for MLS purposes. However, if the person has dependents for MLS purposes of their own, those dependents must be covered by an appropriate level of private patient hospital cover under a complying private health insurance policy for the person to not be liable for the MLS.
As dependant persons aren’t able to claim a private health insurance rebate, they don't get their own PHI statement (tax statement) to evidence they were covered by an appropriate level of private patient hospital cover. Dependants can instead use the PHI statement information from their family (parent/parents), if covered as a dependant person, and update their ‘tax code’ to reflect their circumstances. Refer to the ATO website or refer to the members registered tax accountant.
For example, if you’re single and earning $115,000
No hospital cover
Up to $1150 in Medicare Levy Surcharge
That’s extra tax that you could have avoided if you’d bought hospital cover
Rely on the public hospital system or self-fund your treatment
That could mean long waiting lists, and no choice of doctor or hospital—or if you self-fund, it can mean large out-of-pocket costs
With hospital cover
$0 in Medicare Levy Surcharge (if you hold private hospital cover for the entire financial year)
Put that $1150 towards the cost of your hospital cover—and if all you’re after is the basics, you might even end up with some change in your pocket
Get hospital cover from Australian Unity
Depending on your level of cover that can mean choice of hospital and doctor, scheduling surgery at a time that suits you, and getting a private room (where available)
Do you need to have hospital cover for the full financial year?
The surcharge is payable for every day for which you don’t have hospital cover within the financial year.
This means if you buy hospital cover on 1 July and maintain it throughout the financial year, you won’t pay any Medicare Levy Surcharge. However, if you purchase hospital cover after 1 July, or do not maintain your cover for the full financial year, you’ll pay the surcharge for every day you don’t have hospital cover.
Does everyone in your family need hospital cover?
If you are subject to the Medicare Levy Surcharge and you have a family, everyone in your family, including all dependent children, must have private hospital cover to avoid having to pay the Medicare Levy Surcharge.
Are you covered?
All of Australian Unity’s hospital covers can help you to avoid paying the Medicare Levy Surcharge. (Note that extras only cover does not exempt you from paying the Medicare Levy Surcharge.)

Private health insurance loadings, taxes and rebates

Here’s an overview that helps to explain how these measures work and which ones might help you save money if you have private hospital cover.
Lifetime Health Cover (LHC) loading
If you’re 31 or over, you might have to pay an extra 2% on your hospital cover premiums for each year you’ve gone without private patient hospital cover (after turning 31).

title: Private Health Insurance FAQs
text:
Health Insurance
Private Health Insurance FAQs
About private health insurance
What does private health insurance cover?
There are two types of private health insurance:
Hospital insurance, which covers all or some of the costs of hospital treatment as a private patient including doctor’s charges and hospital accommodation.
Extras insurance (also called ancillary), which covers treatments generally not available under Medicare like dental, optical, physiotherapy, chiropractic and acupuncture.
You can purchase hospital-only insurance, extras-only insurance, or combined hospital plus extras cover.
As a general rule, the more expensive the health cover you choose, the more hospital procedures and extras treatments will be included and the more money you’ll get back when you claim.
Why should I buy private health insurance?
Private health insurance offers you increased choice, convenience and flexibility.
With private hospital cover, you can be treated in a private or public hospital as a private patient. That means that you may be able to choose the doctor that treats you, the hospital you are treated in, and a time for treatment that suits you.
Private insurance also provides “extras” cover for services generally not included under Medicare like dental, optical, physiotherapy, chiropractic, remedial massage and acupuncture. Many people use their private health cover to get access to services they may otherwise not be able to afford.
And last, but certainly not least, depending on your income, buying private hospital cover may help you to minimise your tax by avoiding having to pay the Medicare Levy Surcharge (MLS). Single parents and couples (including de facto couples) are subject to family income thresholds.
What isn’t covered by private health insurance?
Private health insurance does not cover medical services provided out-of-hospital that are covered by Medicare. These include things like GP visits, consultations with specialists (in their rooms) and diagnostic imaging and tests.
Private cover also typically excludes things like elective cosmetic surgery and laser eye surgery.
Can I still be treated as a public patient if I have private health insurance?
Yes. If you are admitted to a public hospital, you can choose to be treated as either a private or public patient.
As a public patient, you’ll receive free public hospital services if you’re entitled to Medicare, but will not be able to take advantage of any of your private cover benefits (like choosing your own doctor).
Am I covered as soon as I take out private health insurance?
When you first buy private health insurance, or when you upgrade to a higher level of cover, you may have to wait some time before you are able to claim. These waiting periods apply to both hospital and extras.
Most private health funds recognise the waiting periods you’ve served with your previous insurer. That means that when you transfer to a level of insurance with the same (or lower) level of cover, as long as you transfer within 30 days of leaving your previous fund, you won’t need to re-serve waiting periods that you’ve already completed.
Am I covered for a condition that I had before I took out private health insurance?
If you were ill before you bought private hospital insurance, even if you were unaware of your illness, you’re considered to have a pre-existing condition. That means you’ll need to serve a waiting period before you are covered for any treatment associated with your illness.
A pre-existing condition is any illness, ailment or condition where the signs or symptoms existed up to six months before and on the day you joined your health fund or upgraded your cover, irrespective of whether you were aware of it.
If you make a hospital claim within the first 12 months after joining your health fund, you may be asked to provide a medical report so the fund can determine whether or not the treatment relates to a pre-existing condition.
After you finish serving your waiting period, you’ll receive full benefits under your policy. Most health funds require you to have continuous cover, and may include time served with a previous insurer if your previous policy was for an equal or higher level of cover.
Can a health fund refuse to insure me because I am elderly or chronically ill?
No. Private health insurers are not allowed to refuse membership on the grounds of health status, age or claims history.
And unlike other types of insurance, they must charge everyone the same premium for the same insurance policy. This is called community rating, and it protects you from having to pay higher premiums if you make a claim, get older or get sick. However, you may need to pay an additional government charge, called the Lifetime Health Cover (LHC) levy, if you delay taking out health cover until after the age of 30.
If you are new to health insurance or are switching to a higher level of cover, you may need to serve a waiting period for pre-existing conditions before you can make any claims.
Will private hospital insurance cover 100% of my medical expenses?
The Australian Government sets a schedule of fees (called the Medicare Benefits Schedule or MBS) for treatments by doctors in a hospital or day surgery. Medicare covers you for 75% of this schedule fee and your private health insurer pays the remaining 25%.
A “gap” can occur if your doctor or specialist charges more than the MBS fee. Any amount that isn’t covered by Medicare or your health fund comes out of your pocket.
You can avoid (or reduce) out of pocket costs by choosing a health fund that offers a gap cover scheme. These health funds can provide you with a list of all doctors and specialists who participate in their gap scheme, so that you can choose to be treated by someone who charges either no gap or else a known low gap payment. Talk to your doctor when planning any surgery, and ask whether the gap scheme applies to your case and to make sure that you fully understand what your out-of-pocket costs will be.
Joining a health fund
What should I look for when choosing health insurance?
When it comes to private health insurance, you’ll find that cheapest does not always equal best value. In fact, paying just a little extra each month can actually save you money, because you may be covered for more services that you’ll actually use.
When shopping for outstanding value health insurance, some of the things you should look at include:
What services are included and excluded?
What restrictions apply to your cover?
How much can you get back for the services you’re most likely to use?
What waiting periods apply before you can claim?
How easy is it to make a claim?
Can you still see your favourite doctors and specialists?
Do you still get the same amount back if your doctor/specialist isn’t part of the fund’s preferred “network” of providers?
What private hospitals can you go to?
Is a “gap cover” scheme available?
What excess is payable for hospital visits and how many times each year does an excess apply?
Is it easy to transfer between funds?
Yes. You can change pivate health insurance policies at any time: from one fund to another or even changing to a higher or lower level of cover within the same health fund.
You’ll receive continuous cover if you transfer to Australian Unity within 30 days of leaving your previous fund. And if you switch to an equal (or lower) level of cover, you won’t have to re-serve any waiting periods you’ve already completed.
The old fund will provide your new fund with a transfer certificate, which provides details about your level of cover, waiting periods already served, a history of recent claims, and any Lifetime Health Cover loading that applies.
This information may also be used to adjust the annual and lifetime claim limits on your new policy. For example, if you’ve made $900 worth of orthodontics claims on your old cover, and your new policy has a $2400 lifetime claim limit, that $900 will be deducted from your new policy ($2400 - $900 = $1500) to reflect your true available limit.
Find out more about switching to Australian Unity.
Will I have to serve waiting periods?
When you take out private health insurance for the first time, or when you increase your level of cover (including reducing your excess level), you’ll need to serve a waiting period before you can claim on some treatments.
This helps to keep insurance premiums lower because it stops people from making a large claim shortly after joining, and then cancelling their membership straight away.
The Australian federal government sets the maximum waiting periods that funds can impose for hospital treatment, including 12 months for pre-existing conditions and for obstetrics (pregnancy), and two months for rehabilitation and palliative care.
Do I get my money back if I change my mind and cancel my policy?
When you join any fund or take out a new cover, you have the benefit of a 30-day cooling off period. This means that if you change your mind within the first 30 days after joining, and haven’t made a claim for benefits on the new private health cover, you may get a refund of any contributions you’ve paid.
How often should I review my cover?
It’s a good idea to review your health insurance needs regularly (at least once a year) to make sure the cover you have still fits your circumstances and budget.
This is especially important if your situation changes, for example if you decide to start a family or if someone in your family has developed a health issue.
Can I change the level of cover I have?
Yes. You can change private health insurance policies at any time: from one fund to another or even changing to a higher or lower level of cover within the same health fund.
If you change to a higher level of cover, you will usually need to serve a waiting period before you can claim on the increased services or limits. This includes transferring to covers with a lower level of hospital excess.
Can my health fund change the level of cover I have?
Yes. Your private health fund can change both the price you pay for your policy and also the benefits or the terms and conditions of your policy.
In making these changes, all health funds (including us) are bound by the Australian Consumer Law, the Private Health Insurance Act 2007 and associated rules and the industry Private Health Insurance Code of Conduct.
Premiums usually change once a year on 1 April, and unfortunately due to things like an increase in the cost of healthcare and people living longer, they usually go up.
We may at any time make changes to your cover. This may include adding or reducing the benefits or services available to you.
We will ensure that we provide you with appropriate notice of these changes in accordance with the Private Health Insurance Act 2007, the Australian Consumer Law and the Private Health Insurance Code of Conduct prior to these changes taking effect.
If you do not wish to continue under the changed cover, you have the option of transferring to a different cover or cancelling your membership. If you do cancel, you’re entitled to a refund of any premiums paid in advance
How long can children remain on family policies?
With Australian Unity, you can include your children (including adopted or foster children) as dependants until they turn 31, as long as they are not married or in a de-facto relationship. The type of family health cover you need will depend on whether any children aged between 23-31 are full-time students.
There may be differences in the way that health funds classify dependants, so it’s a good idea to check the details with your chosen fund.
Do I need to organise separate Ambulance cover?
The answer to this one varies depending on what level of private health cover you have and where you live.
Where you are covered for emergency ambulance, you are covered for the transportation to hospital provided that the transport is coded an invoices as an emergency by a State Ambulance authority. In addition, you may be covered for ambulance attendances, where an ambulance comes to you but you are not taken to hospital.
Check your product Fact Sheet for more information about your cover.
Queensland and Tasmania have state-based ambulance schemes where residents are fully covered.
NSW and ACT provide ambulance cover if you have hospital or ambulance-only insurance. Send any ambulance accounts to your health fund, who will then approve and forward the accounts to the applicable ambulance transport scheme.
For everyone else, we recommend that you purchase an ambulance subscription with your applicable State Ambulance provider (where available) so that you’re covered in non-emergency situations.
What should I do if I feel that my health fund is treating me unfairly?
If you are unhappy with any aspect of the services you receive from your health fund, the first step is to contact the health fund directly to try and resolve the issue. You can find out more about Australian Unity’s complaint resolution process here.
If you are not able to resolve the issue with your health fund, you can contact the Private Health Insurance Ombudsman (PHIO).
The PHIO is an independent office, appointed by the Federal Government, whose services are free to all health fund members. The Ombudsman handles enquiries, suggestions and complaints, and will assist you in resolving a dispute. You can find out more on the PHIO website at ombudsman.gov.au.
Surcharges, loadings and rebates
Can I receive the Australian Government Rebate on Private Health Insurance?
Most Australians are eligible to receive a rebate from the Australian Government to help reduce the cost of their health cover (for both hospital and extras covers).
The rebate amount varies depending on eligibility, age and income levels, with levels being adjusted by the government on 1 April each year.
Do I have to pay the Lifetime Health Cover (LHC) loading?
If you're 31 or over, you might have to pay an extra 2% loading for each year you've gone without hospital cover.
The Lifetime Health Cover (LHC) loading was introduced by the Australian Government in July 2000 to encourage people to take out private hospital insurance at a younger age and maintain it over time.
Find out whether LHC affects you.
I’ve recently immigrated to Australia. Do I have to pay LHC loading?
As a new migrant to Australia, you can avoid paying the LHC loading by taking out private hospital cover before 1 July following your 31st birthday or before the first anniversary of your full Medicare registration (that is, when you are eligible for a blue or green Medicare card).
If you miss the 1 July cut-off date, you will have to pay 2% more for each year you are aged over 30 when you take out comprehensive private health insurance.
Find out more about LHC.
Do I have to pay the Medicare Levy Surcharge (MLS)?
Depending on your income, buying private hospital cover may help you to minimise your tax by avoiding having to pay the Medicare Levy Surcharge (MLS). Single parents and couples (including de facto couples) are subject to family income thresholds.
If it applies to you, the MLS adds a surcharge of between 1% and 1.5% of your income* to your tax liability if you don’t have private hospital cover.
The MLS is calculated on a daily rate, so if you have private hospital cover for only part of the financial year, you may have to pay MLS for the remaining part of the year. Find out more about the Medicare Levy Surcharge.
*For more information, visit the ATO website.
Do I still have to pay the Medicare Levy if I have private health insurance?
Most Australians pay 2% of their taxable income towards the Medicare Levy, which is used to help fund our public health system. This is a levy that must be paid, regardless of whether you have private health cover in Australia.
The federal government uses this money to pay for health services including:
GP visits, consultations with specialists (in their rooms) and diagnostic imaging and tests—none of which are covered by private insurance
Hospital treatments and accommodations, paying 100% of the scheduled fees for public patients, and 75% for private patients (who have the remaining 25% paid for by their private insurer)
The Medicare Levy Surcharge (MLS) is an additional amount (on top of the 2%) that is charged to higher income earners if they don’t have private hospital insurance.
Using your cover
When do I have to pay an excess/co-payment?
Depending on your level of cover, you may need to pay an excess and/or co-payments for your hospital admission. These are an amount you agree to pay upfront towards your hospital cost, in exchange for a lower premium for the cover.
Check your policy to see the excess details for your hospital cover:
Generally excesses will apply once per person admitted to hospital per calendar year
Co-payments apply per day, and may be capped up to a maximum amount per admission
Excesses and co-payments may be waived for dependant admissions, Accident related admissions or same day procedures - refer to your product Fact Sheet.
Excesses are only ever payable if you are hospitalised. They do not apply to extras.
Am I still covered if I fall behind in my payments?
That depends on how far behind you fall.
If you owe less than 60 days, Australian Unity will allow you to pay your outstanding contributions and maintain continuity of cover. That means your private health insurance will be considered to be continuous during the period.
After 60 days your membership is considered to have lapsed and you will no longer be covered.
Am I covered if I go overseas?
No, your Australian private health insurance is only effective in Australia.
We recommend that you take out travel insurance whenever you travel overseas. The good news is that as an Australian Unity member, you’re entitled to a 10% discount on travel insurance.
Can I suspend my cover if I go overseas (so that I don’t have to re-serve waiting periods)?
Yes. Australian Unity members with hospital cover (or hospital + extras cover) can suspend their membership if they go overseas for two months or more, and then reinstate it when they return without having to re-serve waiting periods.
You must have been an Australian Unity member for at least 1 month, and can suspend your membership for a minimum of 2 months and maximum of 24 months.
Find out more about suspending your membership.
Can someone else manage my membership for me?
Yes. If you would like a partner, friend or relative to speak to Australian Unity on your behalf and manage your membership, you can either:
Fill out this delegated authority form
Call us on 1800 760 719
The person you nominate will then be able to access and update your personal information—both over the phone and online. You will remain the only one who can change your level of cover or cancel your insurance.
Where can I find more detailed information about my membership and health cover?
Additional information about Private Health Insurance can be found here. If you can't find the information you're looking for give us a call on 1800 760 719 or email us.
What cover is right for you?
Health insurance is not a one-size-fits-all proposition.
Needs change depending on things like lifestyle, life stage, health issues and financial situations. That means that a single 30-year-old looking for basic hospital and extras cover will have a different list of requirements to a young couple planning on having their first child.
Choosing health cover can be confusing and even a bit overwhelming. That’s why most health funds provide tools on their websites to help you choose the cover that’s right for you. Or if you prefer to talk to someone, you can get advice over the phone. (You can call Australian Unity on 1800 760 719.)

title: How to claim on Health Insurance
text:
Health Insurance
How to make a claim
How to claim on Health Insurance
Choose the type of service or treatment you want to claim for:
Extras treatment
Claim on extras treatments
Extras treatments include things like dental, optical, physiotherapy, remedial massage, acupuncture and others.
Not sure which extras you can claim on or how much you can claim? Log into Online Member Services or check your Fact Sheet to find out what’s included for your cover.
How to claim
On the spot
It's easy as 1, 2, 3...
1. Visit Provider
2. Swipe your card
3. Claim processed
If your extras provider has a HICAPS or CSC machine, simply swipe your Australian Unity membership card on the spot.
Once your claim is authorised, you simply pay any difference between the Australian Unity benefit and your provider’s fee.
Did you know?
If you don’t have a membership card, you can order a replacement using our Online Member Services today.
Order a new card
Claim on the App
Log into your Australian Unity health app.
Tap 'Claims’, then ‘Submit Claim’.
Select your type of service, then upload your itemised invoice from the provider and any other documents required to support your claim.
Once we’ve processed your claim, we’ll make a payment into your nominated bank or credit union account.
Claim online
Log into your Online Member Services account.
Head to ‘Make a claim’ and select ‘Extras services’.
App or online
Log into your Australian Unity health app or Online Member Services (online account).
If you are in Online Member Services, Head to ‘Make a claim’ and select ‘Extras services’. If you are in the app, tap 'Claims’, then ‘Submit Claim’.
Once we’ve processed your claim, we’ll make a payment into your nominated bank or credit union account. If you haven’t paid your provider, it will be your responsibility to pass it on.
If there’s any amount outstanding after our payment to you, you’ll need to pay this.
Mail email or fax
Complete a health cover claim form.
Attach your itemised invoice from your health service provider, and any other documents that are required to support your claim.
Send it all to Australian Unity. You can find the reply-paid postal address and email address on the claim form.
What you'll need to make a claim
Unless you can claim on the spot, you'll need to provide evidence to support your claim. For extras claims, we need to see an itemised invoice for the service you received. It cannot be more than 2 years old.
The invoice must include:
the name of the person who received the service
date of service and type of service, plus item number if relevant
provider’s name and practice address
at least one of the following:
provider number
provider phone number
practice name
provider’s association number or ABN
For some claims - including preventative health, sickness travel and accommodation benefits, and items like orthotics or TENS machines—you may need to provide different documentation to support your claim.
Manage your health insurance with ease
The Australian Unity mobile app makes it a breeze to manage your health insurance.
What's required to make a claim for extras
Orthotics
An invoice, which includes the name of the person the item was for and details of where it was purchased.
A referral letter from an approved healthcare practitioner for the item, or for the referral details to be included on the invoice.
Preventative Health Services & Healthy Lifestyle
An invoice, which includes the name of the person who received the service/program.
A completed preventative health cover claim form.
A referral letter from an approved healthcare practitioner where required.
TENS machine
An invoice for the purchase (or repair of an existing device). It must include the name of the person the item was for and details of where it was purchased (or repaired).
A referral letter from an approved healthcare practitioner, or for the referral details to be included on the invoice.
CPAP or BPAP
An invoice for the purchase (or repair of an existing device), which includes the name of the person the item was for and details of where it was purchased (or repaired).
Health management services
An invoice, which includes the name of the person who participated in the support program.
A letter from a healthcare practitioner may be required, explaining that the activity is to improve an illness or condition. This letter must include the type of illness or condition. (No letter is required for birth and lactation classes, and diabetes education.)
Sickness travel and accommodation benefits
Itemised receipts or bills relating to the travel and accommodation.
When claiming for ‘Travel, sickness and accommodation’, a letter from a healthcare practitioner describing the travel and accommodation as necessary for the required treatment.
Braces, splints and garments
An invoice for the purchase, which includes the name of the person the item was for and details of where it was purchased.
For garments, we may request a letter from a healthcare practitioner explaining the condition for which the item is required, or for the referral details to be included on the invoice. Please see your Fact Sheet or contact us for more details on whether a referral is required.

Claim on hospital procedures
The hospital procedures (including day surgeries) that you can claim on will vary depending on your level of cover.
Not sure which hospital procedures you can claim on? Log into your account or check your Fact Sheet to view details about your health cover.
Before booking treatment, you should contact us to ask about the benefits you can expect to receive and any out-of-pocket expenses you might incur.
What's required to make a claim for hospital procedures
Accommodation and theatre fees
You shouldn’t be charged for accommodation or theatre fees (or prosthesis, if needed) if you’re “Covered” for your procedure at that hospital (your Fact Sheet will tell you which treatments are “Covered” and at which type of hospital); and you’ve completed any applicable waiting periods.
In most cases, the hospital will bill Australian Unity directly. You’ll only receive an invoice if an excess or co-payment applies to your cover (and you haven’t already paid it). If you do happen to receive an invoice for the full amount, please call us on 13 29 39.
If your procedure is “Covered” but is in a “non-agreement” private hospital or a private room of a public hospital, you may incur large out-of-pocket costs. This may include theatre fees, intensive or coronary care costs and accommodation. If your cover provides for “Restricted” benefits, Australian Unity will only pay the basic default benefit for your accommodation and prosthesis (if needed). You will not be covered for any other accommodation and theatre fee costs relating to your procedure, and may incur large out-of-pocket costs. For medical costs, see below.
For any charges not covered by Australian Unity, you will need to contact the hospital and confirm how to pay.
Medical costs
The way you claim the bills from your surgeons and other doctors will vary depending on whether they’re participating in Australian Unity’s Gap Cover scheme.
If your policy includes Gap Cover - and your doctor agrees to participate in the scheme for your procedure—they should deal directly with Medicare and Australian Unity. You should only receive an invoice from them if there are out-of-pocket costs (which can still arise, depending on how much your doctor charges). These costs are not covered by Australian Unity. It’s the responsibility of your treating doctor and hospital to advise you of potential out-of-pocket costs before you’re admitted into hospital. If they don’t provide an estimate of those costs, it is your right to ask for informed financial consent.
Ways to claim for non Gap Cover claims
If your doctor isn’t participating in Gap Cover, you’ll receive an invoice from them. You can either claim your Australian Unity benefits through Medicare or come to us. Either way, you’ll still need to go to Medicare first.
Claim through Medicare
You can submit a Medicare Two-way claim form to Medicare. If payable, Medicare will process its part of the claim and organise payment to you. Medicare will then forward the details to Australian Unity so we can process our part of the claim. We’ll make any payment into your nominated bank or credit union account.
Online
Submit your paperwork to Medicare. You’ll receive a cheque, or some other form of payment, for your doctor and a statement of Medicare benefits for Australian Unity.
Hold onto the payment from Medicare. Then log into Online Member Services (online account).
Head to ‘Make a claim’ and select ‘Medical services’. Complete the online form. Make sure to include your statement of Medicare benefits and any other documents relevant to your claim.
Pass the payment from Australian Unity, and the Medicare payment, onto your doctor. If there’s any amount outstanding, you’ll also need to pay this.
Mail or email
Complete a health cover claim form. Attach your statement of Medicare benefits to the form.
Mail or email the completed form and other documents to Australian Unity. You can find the reply-paid postal address and email address on the claim form.
If there’s any amount outstanding, you’ll need to pay this.
For all claims
If you’re sending documents by mail, please send us copies and keep the originals for your own records, as Australian Unity will not return originals.

Hospital + extras (including combination covers)

If you have more than one extras policy, you can only access your most recent extras policy in the app. For subsequent extras policies, and to claim for hospital or other services, you can use Online Member Service portal via mobile or desktop.
The app will initially not be available for policies without extras, including;
Hospital only

Members with these policies can still use Online Member Service portal via mobile or desktop, to make claims, update details and more.

title: Suspending your private health insurance
text:
Health Insurance
Using your cover
Suspending your cover
Suspending your private health insurance
If you’ve got hospital cover with Australian Unity, you can suspend your membership under certain conditions and reinstate it later without having to re-serve any of the waiting periods that you’ve already completed.
You won’t pay any premiums during the time your cover is suspended, but you also won’t be able to claim on any hospital or extras services you have during the suspension period.
The suspension applies to the whole membership, and all members listed on the policy will not be insured during the suspension period.
If you hold hospital and extras products under the same membership you can’t suspend one without the other.
The fund has the right deny the suspension request if your request does not meet the suspension requirements. We recommend your communication preference is set to email, this will ensure you have access to all correspondence including confirmation or denial details of your suspension whilst your Membership is suspended.
Contact Australian Unity on 13 29 39 if you have any questions about suspending your level of cover.
If you’ve got Overseas Visitors Cover, you can check whether you’re eligible to suspend your cover here.
If you’re travelling overseas
You can suspend your cover for overseas travel if:
You have been an Australian Unity member with hospital cover (including combined hospital and extras cover) for at least 1 month.
The minimum suspension period is 2 months with a maximum suspension period of 24 months.
The membership must be paid up to or in advance of the proposed effective date of the suspension.
If you suspend your cover, you will not be able to suspend it again until 12 months after the date of resumption.
Members with separate hospital and extras memberships will need to suspend both simultaneously.
If you’re suffering financial hardship
You can suspend your cover for financial hardship if:
you've been an Australian Unity member with hospital cover (including combined hospital and extras cover) for 12 continuous months
your membership is paid up to your suspension date
Your cover can be suspended for financial hardship up to a maximum of three times over the lifetime of your membership, with each suspension being a maximum of three months. A minimum of 12 months must have passed since your last suspension.
14 week paid parental leave and access to our Bump to Baby program
Accessible Employee Assistance Program
Attractive employee discounts on Australian Unity Health and General Insurance
Join a supportive and friendly team
How to reinstate your cover
Unless we hear from you, your cover will automatically be reinstated on the date approved by Australian Unity for your suspension request.
Once your membership is reinstated, all benefits and waiting periods will resume from where they left off
When your membership is reinstated we will credit any payments made in advance of your suspension date.
If you were paying by direct debit before suspending your membership, you’ll need to contact Australian Unity to get your direct debit reinstated when you come back to Australia.
Your membership (and all benefit entitlements) will cease if your membership becomes unfinancial due to failure to make a further payment after its reinstatement.
Important things to know
You’re not covered while your membership is suspended
Australian Unity will not pay for any hospital or extras services during the suspension period.
How does the suspension affect Lifetime Health Cover (LHC) loading?
If you suspend your membership instead of cancelling it, you will not pay any additional LHC loading on your hospital cover when you reinstate your cover. You can find out more about LHC loading at www.australianunity.com.au/lhc
Note: If you have LHC loading, the 10 year anniversary end date will be delayed by the period your membership was suspended.
How does suspension affect the Medicare Levy Surcharge (MLS)?
If you suspend your membership, you may no longer be exempt from the Medicare Levy Surcharge. Speak to your accountant or the Australian Tax Office to find out if this possible additional tax could outweigh what you’ll save. You can find out more about the MLS at www.australianunity.com.au/mls

title: Setting up a Delegated Authority
text:
Health Insurance
Using your cover
Delegated authority setup
Setting up a Delegated Authority
We take your privacy seriously, which is why Australian Unity has strict security measures in place to protect your personal information. That means we will deal ONLY with you, as the policy holder, or your partner on the policy (unless you tell us otherwise) in all matters related to your Private Health Insurance membership.
Partner Delegated Authority
Unless you tell us otherwise, a partner or spouse included on your policy, will have automatic delegated authority on your policy.
Delegated authority gives your partner or spouse the authority to do anything you could do as the policyholder except cancel the policy, change the policyholder, remove the policyholder from the policy or nominate further delegated authorities. This means your partner or spouse will have authorisation to act on your behalf to access and discuss personal information (including claims information) about all members covered under the policy and to make changes to the policy e.g. change the level of the cover or contact details, add or remove a dependant or suspend the policy.
If you have a partner or spouse on your policy and don’t want them to be given delegated authority you can cancel the delegated authority by contacting us on 13 29 39 Monday - Friday 8:30am - 6:00pm AET excluding public holidays.
If you’d like to authorise another person to speak to Australian Unity on your behalf and to help manage your membership, you can set up a Delegated Authority. For example:
You can add an authority for an adult family member or friend to discuss your membership
If you have family members who are looked after by a carer, you can add authority for their carer to speak to us directly
What is covered by a Delegated Authority?
The person you name as a Delegated Authority can make enquiries about, and changes to, most aspects of your membership. They will have the authority to do anything you can do as the policyholder except cancel the policy, change the policyholder, remove the policyholder from the policy or nominate further delegated authorities.
Policy Holder | Delegated Authority/Partner on Policy
Change personal details including address and phone number | Yes
Enquire about policy details and level of cover | Yes
Change your level of cover | Yes
Make a payment | Yes
Change payment method | Yes | Yes*
Add or remove a dependent | Yes
Make a claim | Yes
Enquire about the progress of a claim | Yes
Suspend your membership | Yes
Cancel your membership | Yes | No
Change or remove the Policyholder | Yes | No
Add or remove a Delegated Authority | Yes | No
*New direct debits need to be made from your Delegated Authority’s account
How do you set up a Delegated Authority?
Simply complete the Delegated Authority Form and return it to Australian Unity.
When completing the form, make sure that you:
Include the name of the person who will be looking after your health insurance matters
Sign the form
Still got questions?
Find the answers to your questions below
Call us at 13 29 39 Monday - Friday 8:30am - 6:00pm AET excluding public holidays or simply complete the Delegated Authority Form and return it to Australian Unity.
Removing a Delegated Authority
You can remove a Delegated Authority, including partner authority at any time by simply contacting Australian Unity on 13 29 39.

Access your digital card so you can easily tap and claim at your healthcare provider from your iPhone¹ or Android² smartphone—useful for everything you do.
How to download the Australian Unity Health App
Next time you visit a participating extras provider, follow these steps to tap and claim on the spot.
Step 1
Download the app from the App Store or Google Play.
Step 2
Register or log in using your email password.
Step 3
Enter the code we send to you via SMS to verify your identity.
Tap. Claim. Worth it.
Keep your member card handy wherever you go and make instant claims using your digital card on Android and Apple devices.
Find out more
Popular questions
Who can use the app?
The app can be used by members who have:
Hospital & extras
Extras cover only
Overseas visitor cover & extras
The app does not currently support the following policies:
Hospital cover only
Overseas visitor cover only
Members who have Hospital cover only, or Overseas visitor cover only will be redirected to the browser-based member portal to manage their accounts.
Members who hold multiple policies will only be able to view their most recently used extra in the app, and they’ll be redirected to the browser-based portal for additional needs.
What is my username?
Your username is the email address you provided when you took out your Australian Unity product or service. If two individuals on your policy share an e-mail address, this will generally be linked to the primary policy holder only.
I have the previous app on my phone. What do I need to do?
Next time you open the app, you'll be prompted to update it.
Your login details have not changed. Simply enter the same username and password and you'll be all set.
If you still have our old app, (from prior to April 2022), you will need to delete it, then visit the app store to download the new app. You’ll also need to re-register for Australian Unity Online Member Services.
How do I register to use my online account?
From the log-in screen, select ‘Using your online account for the first time? Register for access’ and follow the steps.
What happens if I don’t have an email address registered with Australian Unity?
When you complete the registration process to access your online account, you will be required to provide an email address if you have not previously provided one to Australian Unity. This will be verified and will become your username.
What if I forget my username?
Your username is the email address associated with your Australian Unity product or service. If you can’t remember what that is, from the log-in screen, select ‘Forgot email’ and follow the steps to retrieve your email address.
What if I can’t remember my password?
From the log-in screen, select ‘Forgot password’ and follow the steps to reset your password.
How can I change my password?
The easiest way to change your password is to visit the log-in screen, select ‘Forgot password’ and follow the steps.
What happens if I have different email addresses attached to different Australian Unity products or services?
We have processes in place that will determine the most current and reliable email address across the products or services that you have with us If you want to find out which email address is your username, from the log-in screen, select ‘Forgot email’ and follow the steps.
Why is my Australian Unity account locked after I tried to enter my details or password?
To safeguard your information, we lock accounts when there have been too many incorrect attempts to access them. If your account is locked, please try again after 30 minutes.

text:
Health Insurance
Health Insurance member services
Benefits and Discounts
Get the most out of your Health insurance cover
How to get the most out of your private health insurance
Whether you have a high level of cover or just the essentials, here are our top 5 tips for making the most of your health insurance.
Know what you’re covered for
Knowing what you’re covered for is crucial. Health insurance, including extras, covers a wide range of services and treatments. It’s easy to forget just how many. If it’s been a while since you last read your Fact Sheet, then get to it. You may be surprised what you can claim on.
You can view your Fact Sheet via Online Member Services (your online account), by selecting ‘Account details’. It’s the second quick link. You can also access it by going to ‘Your cover’ and scrolling to the bottom of the page.
Use the ‘Get estimate’ tool, which you’ll also find under ‘Your cover’ to see what you might get back on you extras claim.
If you haven’t yet set up your online account, you can register here.
Know your limits and when they reset
When it comes to extras cover, use it or lose it. It’s just that simple!
It’s important you understand how much of your benefits you’ve used and how much you still have left. Our annual extras limits (the benefits you can claim each year) are reset on 1 January every year. So when it’s getting close to the end of the year, check your limits to see how much you have left to use.
By knowing when your limits reset, you can plan any treatments and really maximise your cover.
Check out your extras Product Fact Sheet so you get a clear understanding of what you can and can’t claim for on your cover.
Mind the gap
Our Gap Cover can reduce or remove your out-of-pocket expenses because we set our own schedule of fees, which is generally higher than the Government schedule. When your doctor or specialist agrees to use our Gap Cover Scheme, we can help to pay some or all the gap that can occur if your doctor's charge is higher than the Medicare Benefits Schedule (MBS) fee.
Gap Cover Schemes are available to all doctors who treat private patients in hospitals or day surgeries, but they don't always participate. Doctors are also free to participate in a Gap Cover Scheme on a patient-by-patient basis.
If Gap Cover won’t fully cover your participating doctor’s fees, your doctor must tell you how much you’ll have to pay in writing before treatment can begin. This is called Informed Financial Consent.
You should always ask your doctor if they will participate in the Australian Unity Gap Cover Scheme for your service prior to undergoing treatment. Not all covers have Gap Cover, so to check your eligibility, please review your Product Fact Sheet. You can also view Gap Cover doctors here.
Get a health cover check-up!
If you haven’t reviewed your private health cover in the past couple of years, it may be well worth your while to do so. Health insurance is not a one-size-fits-all proposition. Needs change depending on things like lifestyle, life stage, health issues and financial situations. In addition, there may be new features or products available that suit your circumstances better.
You can check what you’re covered for and determine if that’s still the right cover for you by visiting Online Member Services or by calling us on 13 29 39.
More benefits of private health cover
As an Australian Unity member, you can get access to a wide range of rewards, discounts, programs and services designed to help you get healthy and stay healthy.
Get more value from your health insurance with Wellplan Rewards where you can save money on everyday things like groceries, petrol and movie tickets.
Or why not be rewarded for telling your friends and family about us. With Member Get Member you’ll receive a $100 gift card* every time a friend you refer joins Australian Unity and takes out Hospital, Combined Hospital and Extras, or Overseas Visitors Cover. Just make sure that they give us your details when they sign up.
If you have any other questions about the added benefits of your health cover you can email us by logging into your Online Member Services or contact us on 13 29 39.
*Only available if the friend you refer has not held active health insurance with Australian Unity in the last 5 years (other than as a child or student dependant). Not available through intermediaries or corporate plans. Cover must be purchased through the Australian Unity call centre or website. See full terms and conditions.

No Gap Dental Network
Here's something to make you smile
Many people don't visit the dentist until a problem arises, such as a severe toothache. By then it's often too late! The condition has developed and it will cost money and perhaps involve significant pain to fix. But preventative care can make all the difference. A regular dental checkup allows your dentist to detect serious conditions before they become a costly problem.
Australian Unity's No Gap Dental service offers members with eligible cover preventative dental treatment at no out-of pocket cost (up to your yearly limit). We are constantly looking for ways to provide better value to our members and our No Gap dental network delivers just that.
Members who visit the dentist regularly for preventative dental treatment, keep their teeth healthier, saving you money in the long run.

The information on this page is a summary only. Please read the product Fact Sheet to understand the benefits, limits, restrictions, exclusions, waiting periods, pre-existing conditions and excesses that apply, and what it means to be 'Covered' including out-of-pocket costs.
Why choose Australian Unity for dental cover?
100% back on check ups
Get 100% back on your 6 monthly check-ups at the dentist, including x-rays and cleans when you use one of our no gap dental providers.1 Find out more
Choose your own provider
Get strong dental benefits outside our dental network as well, we won’t lock you into our network.3
Limits that grow
Depending on the product you choose, you can access limits that get larger the longer you’re with us.
Compare cover
Dental cover at a glance
What is dental cover?
Dental cover is an Extras health insurance benefit that helps pay towards dental treatment, including check-ups, scale and cleans, fillings and, depending on your cover, major dental services such as crowns, extractions, bridges, root canal treatment and dentures.
Can I get dental cover without hospital cover?
Yes. Dental benefits are included in all Australian Unity Extras products, which can be purchased on their own or paired with Hospital cover.
Does Medicare cover dental treatment?
Medicare generally does not cover routine dental treatment for Australian adults.
Understanding the different types of dental cover
Dental benefits are often grouped into preventative dental, general dental and major dental. Understanding the difference can help you choose cover that matches your needs.
Preventative Dental | General Dental | Major Dental
What is it | Regular care that helps maintain oral health and identify issues early. | Common treatments used to repair or treat everyday dental issues. | More complex treatments that can be more expensive.
Examples | Check-ups | Fillings | Crowns
Cleans | Simple extractions e.g. Wisdom teeth removal (If the extraction is simple and not carried out in a hospital) | Bridges
Fluoride treatments | Restorative Services – Adhesive Restorations, such as tooth-coloured fillings and repairs | Dentures
X-rays | Root canal treatment
Dental implants
Regular check-ups and cleans can help identify dental issues early. Putting off dental care may result in more complex treatment, higher out-of-pocket costs and a greater impact on your overall health and wellbeing, particularly as you get older.
Compare cover
Dental cover for orthodontics
Many Australians look for dental cover that helps with orthodontic treatment such as braces and clear aligners, including Invisalign® where eligible. Some Extras products may include orthodontic benefits, subject to annual limits, lifetime limits and waiting periods.
When comparing cover, consider:
yearly orthodontic limits
lifetime orthodontic limits
waiting periods
whether your dentist or provider is recognised to provide orthodontic treatment
Dental jargon explained
Dental cover feature | What it means
No Gap Dental Network# | Participating providers may offer 100% back on eligible preventive dental services on selected products.1
General dental | Routine care such as check-ups, cleans and fillings.
Major dental | More complex treatment such as crowns, bridges, dentures and root canals.
Waiting periods and limits | Rules that affect when and how much members can claim.
FAQs
What is dental cover?
Dental cover is an Extras health insurance benefit that helps pay towards eligible dental treatment. It’s usually included as part of an Extras product alongside other services, rather than being sold as a separate dental-only product.
Is dental cover included in Extras cover?
Dental cover is typically included in Extras cover rather than Hospital cover. Depending on the product, dental benefits may help with preventive, general and major dental services. Australian Unity offers a range of Extras products that include dental benefits.
What dental services are usually covered?
Depending on your product, dental benefits may help with check-ups, cleans, X-rays, fillings and other services such as crowns, bridges, dentures, dental implants and root canals.
Yes. Australian Unity offers Extras cover options that include dental benefits without requiring Hospital cover.
Many people choose Extras-only cover when they want help with dental, optical, physiotherapy and other common healthcare services.
Is dental cover worth it?
It may be worth considering if you want help managing the cost of routine or future dental treatment.
How much does dental cover cost?
The cost of dental cover depends on the type of Extras cover you choose, your age, location and level of benefits. Generally, products with higher annual limits and dental benefits cost more than entry-level cover. When comparing options, consider both the premium you pay and the benefits and limits available to you.
Can I get dental cover without waiting periods?
Waiting periods may apply for dental services depending on the treatment and product selected. If you're switching from another insurer and have already served equivalent waiting periods, you generally won't need to serve them again.
Does health insurance cover major dental treatment?
Some Extras products include benefits towards major dental treatment. Major dental may include services such as crowns, bridges, dentures, root canal treatment and dental implants, depending on your level of cover. Benefits, annual limits and waiting periods can vary, so it's important to check the product details.
Does health insurance cover orthodontics?
Some Extras health insurance products include benefits for orthodontic treatment, such as braces and other corrective dental services. Cover levels, annual limits, lifetime limits and waiting periods can vary, so it's important to compare product features if orthodontic treatment is likely to be important for you or your family.
Does health insurance cover Invisalign®?
Some Extras products may provide benefits towards clear aligners, such as Invisalign® treatment, where orthodontic services are included under the policy. Benefits, limits, eligibility requirements and waiting periods will depend on the product selected. Always check the relevant product information before starting treatment.
What should I look for when choosing dental cover?
When comparing dental cover, consider:
The types of dental services covered, such as preventive, general, major dental and orthodontics.
Annual limits, sub limits(a smaller limit that applies within the broader overall limit), family limits and any lifetime limits that apply.
Waiting periods before benefits can be claimed.
Whether there is access to a preferred or no-gap dental provider network.
The expected out-of-pocket costs for treatment.
Whether the product offers enough value for your expected dental needs and budget.
Does health insurance cover dental implants?
Some Extras products include benefits towards dental implants under major dental. Cover, annual limits and waiting periods can vary depending on the product you choose. If you're considering dental implants, it's important to review the product details to understand what benefits may be available before commencing treatment.
Can couples and families share dental benefits?
Yes. Couples and families can be on the same Extras policy and receive the same benefits. This depends on the product. It is worth noting that some Extras products apply limits per person, while others may apply a shared limit across a couple or family policy. Understanding how limits apply can help you choose cover that suits the dental needs of your household.
What is the No Gap Dental Network?
It is Australian Unity’s network of participating dental providers where eligible members on selected products receive 100% back on preventive dental services. Things like cleans, check ups and x-rays, which could save you hundreds of dollars. Find out more.
Can I still choose my own dentist?
Yes. With Australian Unity you can claim benefits at any recognised dentist, subject to your cover. Network providers may offer additional value on selected products. In fact, with Australian Unity we know your dentist is important, so we offer great benefits no matter which dentist you want to see.
What does 100% back on preventive dental mean?
It means preventive dental services will be fully covered at participating No Gap Dental Network# providers, this is available on most Australian Unity Extras products, subject to limits, eligibility and waiting periods. That means no, out of pocket costs.
What is general dental?
General dental usually includes routine treatment such as check-ups, X-rays, fillings or simple extractions.
What is major dental?
Major dental generally includes more complex treatment such as crowns, bridges and dentures. It can also include root canal and gum disease treatment and surgical exactions.
Does dental cover include dentures?
Some products include benefits for dentures. At Australian Unity we specify in the product fact sheet when dentures are included Check the product fact sheet for limits and waiting periods.
Does dental cover include crowns?
Some products include benefits for crowns. At Australian Unity we specify in the product fact sheet when crowns are included. Check the product fact sheet for limits and waiting periods.
Does dental cover include root canal treatment?
Some products include benefits for root canal treatment. At Australian Unity we specify in the product fact sheet when root canals are included Check the product fact sheet for limits and waiting periods.
Are there waiting periods for dental cover?
Waiting periods may apply depending on your cover, the dental service and whether you’re new to private health insurance or switching from another fund. If there is a break in cover or you upgrade to higher benefits, waiting periods may apply.
Does Medicare cover dental?
Medicare generally does not cover most routine adult dental services. Some public dental programs may be available depending on eligibility.
Which Australian Unity Extras products include dental?
All Australian Unity Extras products include dental benefits, with the services, benefits and limits varying depending on the product selected..
How do I compare dental cover?
You can compare Australian Unity Extras options online or by speaking with one of our consultants to help choose cover based on your dental needs and budget. When comparing cover between funds look at the included services(preventative, general, major, orthodontic), annual limits, waiting periods, provider network access and how often you expect to use dental services.
How can I get more value from my dental cover?
Check your annual limits, keep up with preventive appointments, use participating No Gap Dental Network# providers where appropriate and review your cover as needs change.

Optical cover at a glance
What is optical cover?
Optical cover is a benefit available through extras health insurance that helps pay for approved vision-related products, such as prescription glasses and contact lenses.
Optical benefits are subject to annual limits , which vary by product and level of cover. Once eligible members have served any applicable waiting periods, they can claim benefits for eligible products up to their available limit.
Can I get optical cover without hospital cover?
Yes. Australian Unity offers Extras cover options that include optical benefits without requiring Hospital cover
Does Medicare cover Optical treatment?
Medicare generally covers eye tests, but it does not usually cover optical products such as glasses, prescription lenses, frames, or contact lenses

Optical and dental cover in one extras policy
Many Australians use optical and dental services regularly, which is why these benefits are commonly packaged together within extras cover.
How to choose the best optical cover
The best optical cover depends on your needs.
Consider optical cover if you:
Wear Prescription Glasses
You may benefit from annual optical claims if you replace your frames or lenses regularly.
Wear Contact Lenses
Contact lens users often look for higher annual limits.
Need prescription sunglasses
Optical cover includes prescription sunglasses.
Use Multiple Extras Services
If you claim on dental, physio and optical each year, a broader extras policy may deliver more value.
Things to look for when comparing:
Annual optical limit
This determines how much you can claim up to. E.g. $200, $250
Waiting periods

Benefits

FAQs
Does health insurance cover glasses?
Many extras policies provide benefits towards prescription glasses, subject to annual limits.
What does optical extras cover include?
Optical extras cover may help pay for:
Purchases of glasses, including lenses and frames, and contact lenses. These must be prescribed by an optometrist or ophthalmologist and supplied in private practice.
Prescription eyewear, such as swim goggles, ski or diving masks, and sunglasses.
Low vision aids and dyslexia-tint glasses, when dispensed by a registered optometrist or oculist.
Can optical cover help pay for contact lenses?
Yes, when optical is included on an Australian Unity product it includes benefits for contact lenses.
Does optical cover include prescription sunglasses?
Yes, when optical is included on an Australian Unity product it includes prescription sunglasses, limits apply.
Can I get dental and optical cover together?
Yes. Dental and optical benefits are commonly included within extras health insurance products.
What is private optical cover?
Private optical cover generally refers to optical benefits provided through private health insurance extras cover.
Are there waiting periods for optical cover?
Yes. A waiting period applies before you can claim optical benefits. If you transfer from another registered Australian health fund, Australian Unity may recognise equivalent waiting periods already served, subject to transfer rules.
Can I switch health funds without serving waiting periods again?
If you're switching from a comparable level of cover, waiting period recognition applies and you don’t have to re-serve those waiting periods.
How do annual optical limits work?
An annual optical limit is the maximum amount that can be claimed for eligible optical services and products each calendar year.
What should I compare when choosing optical cover?
When choosing optical cover, compare the optical benefits, annual limits, waiting periods, overall extras benefits and premium costs.
Is optical cover worth it if I wear glasses every day?
Whether optical cover is worth it depends on your individual needs. If you regularly purchase prescription glasses, contact lenses or other eligible optical products, extras cover with optical benefits may help reduce your out-of-pocket costs.
What is the best optical cover?
The best optical cover depends on your health needs, budget how often you expect to claim, and the range of extras services you use each year.
Is Optical Cover Worth It?
Yes, optical cover may be worth considering if you regularly buy prescription glasses, contact lenses or other eligible optical products.
Can I get optical cover with no waiting period?
You may be able to access optical cover without serving a new waiting period if Australian Unity recognises equivalent waiting periods already served with another registered Australian health fund, subject to transfer rules. Otherwise, a waiting period applies before you can claim optical benefits.
Why choose dental and optical cover together?
Dental and optical cover are commonly included in extras health insurance because they are among the most frequently claimed healthcare services in Australia. Combining dental and optical cover can help reduce the cost of routine dental check-ups, glasses, contact lenses and other eligible treatments through one policy.
How much can I claim for glasses each year?
The amount you can claim for glasses depends on your level of extras cover and your available annual optical limit. Higher levels of cover typically provide higher annual optical benefits. This could be $200, $250 or even $300 depending on your product.
What are optical benefit limits?
An optical benefit limit is the maximum amount you can claim for eligible optical products during a year. Once the limit has been reached, additional claims are generally not payable until the benefit period resets. Australian Unity benefits are reset on the 1st of January each year.
How long is the waiting period for optical cover?
Australian Unity has a 6 month waiting period. However, you may be able to access optical cover without serving a new waiting period if Australian Unity recognises equivalent waiting periods already served with another registered Australian health fund, subject to transfer rules.
Does optical cover include eye tests?
Medicare may cover eligible eye tests when clinically required. Optical cover through private health insurance is used for eligible optical products, such as prescription glasses, contact lenses and prescription sunglasses.
Can I claim designer glasses through health insurance?
Yes as long as they are prescription glasses, you can claim on designer frames, provided the purchase meets eligibility requirements and falls within available optical limits.

Why choose Australian Unity for physio cover?
Freedom to Choose Your Own Physio
You are not restricted to a preferred provider network. You can visit a recognised physiotherapist in private practice and claim eligible benefits according to your cover.
Flexible Cover To Match Your Needs
Choose from a range of Extras options with different benefit levels and annual limits to suit your health needs and budget.
More Than Just Standard Physio

Compare cover
Physio cover at a glance
What is physiotherapy?
Physiotherapy helps improve mobility, manage pain, prevent injuries and support recovery after illness, injury or surgery.
A physiotherapist assesses how your body moves and develops treatment plans that may include:
Exercise programs
Manual therapy
Rehabilitation programs
Strength and mobility training
Injury management
Post-surgical recovery support
Can I get physio cover without hospital cover?
Yes. Australian Unity offers Extras cover options that include physiotherapy benefits without requiring Hospital cover. Hospital cover with Australian Unity may also give eligible members access to physiotherapy support programs, such as Kieser, where the relevant Hospital cover includes joint replacement.
What does physiotherapy cover help pay for?
Physio benefits may help contribute towards the cost of treatment for:
Back pain
Neck pain
Shoulder injuries
Sports injuries
Joint pain
Arthritis management
Mobility issues
Post-surgery rehabilitation
Exercise-based treatment programs
Benefits are subject to your level of cover, annual limits, waiting periods and recognised provider requirements.
Physiotherapy through private health insurance vs Medicare
Medicare may help cover a limited number of physiotherapy visits for people with a chronic condition through a GP Management Plan or Team Care Arrangement. Private health insurance with physiotherapy cover can help contribute towards the cost of ongoing physio treatment beyond Medicare arrangements, up to your cover limits.
Medicare | Extras cover with physio
Who can use it | Those with a chronic illness | Members with eligible Extras cover, subject to waiting periods, annual limits and recognised provider requirements
Other criteria | A number of criteria must be met, including having a chronic condition that has lasted, or is likely to last, at least 6 months and having a formal plan from a GP | A waiting period applies before you can claim physiotherapy benefits. Transfer arrangements may recognise equivalent waiting periods already served.
Benefit | Max 5 sessions | Depends on the cover you have selected e.g. 60% back up to $400
Compare cover
FAQs
Does Australian Unity health insurance cover physiotherapy?
Yes. Physiotherapy benefits are included in Australian Unity products that include Extras cover. The amount you can claim depends on your level of cover, benefit amount, annual limits and remaining benefits.
How does health insurance with physiotherapy work?
You pay for treatment and claim benefits according to your cover, limits and eligibility requirements. E.g. if your physio consult costs $100 and you get 60% back you will receive $60 every consult until your annual limit runs out.
Is physiotherapy covered by Medicare?
Medicare may cover a limited number of allied health visits, including physiotherapy, through a GP Management Plan for eligible people. If a physiotherapy service is eligible to be claimed as an outpatient Medicare service, you cannot also claim a private health insurance benefit for the same service. Ask your provider which claiming pathway applies before the claim is submitted.
Why take out cover for physiotherapy?
It can help reduce the cost of treatment and support ongoing health and recovery needs.
What physiotherapy services does health insurance cover?
It can help pay towards the cost of treatment for injuries, pain, mobility issues and rehabilitation through a physio. This can include appointments for things like back and neck pain, sports injuries, post-surgery recovery and exercise-based treatment plans.
What is the waiting period for physiotherapy?
A 2 month waiting period applies before you can claim physiotherapy benefits. If you transfer from another registered Australian health fund, Australian Unity may recognise equivalent waiting periods already served, subject to transfer rules.
How much can I claim on physiotherapy and are there limits?
The amount you can claim depends on your level of cover. Most policies have a benefit per visit and an annual limit. For example, if your cover pays 60% back up to $400 per year, and your physiotherapy appointment costs $100, you could claim $60 back. Once you reach your annual limit of $400, no further benefits would be payable until your limits reset on 1 January the following year.
Does health insurance cover treatment from any physiotherapist?
Australian Unity gives you the flexibility to choose your own physiotherapist, provided they are recognised by Australian Unity for the service being claimed. Other health funds may have preferred provider networks that can influence where members choose to receive treatment.
Can I choose my own physiotherapist?
Australian Unity allows members to choose their own physiotherapist, provided the physiotherapist is recognised by Australian Unity for the service being claimed and provides services in private practice.
Who should consider getting private health insurance for physiotherapy?
Physiotherapy benefits may be useful if you have ongoing treatment needs, recurring injuries or want help with the cost of future appointments.
How many physio visits are covered with Australian Unity Extras?
The number of visits depends on your benefit amount, annual limits and treatment costs.
How do I check if my physiotherapist is recognised by Australian Unity?
Before booking, contact Australian Unity or ask the physiotherapy clinic whether the provider is recognised by Australian Unity for physiotherapy claims. Benefits are only payable for eligible services from recognised providers.
What happens when I reach my annual limits?
Once your annual limit is reached, no further benefits will be payable until your benefits reset on 1 January the following year. This means you’ll need to pay the full provider charge for any further treatment during that time.
What types of consultations are covered?
You may be able to claim benefits for eligible physiotherapy consultations, including sports physiotherapy and hydrotherapy, subject to your cover, annual limits, waiting periods and recognised provider requirements.
Why choose Australian Unity Extras for physiotherapy?
Australian Unity gives you choice across different levels of physiotherapy benefits, from 50% back up to $300 a year on Easy Extras, through to $70 back per consultation up to $600 a year on Top Extras. You can also choose your own recognised physiotherapist, with benefits subject to your cover, annual limits, waiting periods and recognised provider requirements.
How do I claim for physiotherapy?
Claiming is simple:
Attend your appointment with a recognised physiotherapist in private practice.
Tap your membership card on the HICAPS machine to claim on the spot.
Receive benefits based on your level of cover and remaining annual limits on the spot.
Pay the difference
Alternatively, you can:
Pay for your treatment.
Claim using the Australian Unity app or online member services portal
Receive benefits based on your level of cover and remaining annual limits.
How much does physiotherapy cost?
The cost of physiotherapy can vary depending on the clinic, location and type of treatment. Initial appointments are often more expensive than follow-up visits. Australian Unity Extras cover with physiotherapy benefits can help reduce your out-of-pocket costs.
Does Australian Unity Extras cover physiotherapy?
Yes. Physiotherapy is included in all Australian Unity Extras covers. The amount you can claim will depend on your level of cover, benefit amount and annual limits.
Can I claim physiotherapy straight away?
Is remedial massage covered under physiotherapy?
No. Remedial massage is a separate service and has its own benefits. However, both physiotherapy and remedial massage are often included under the same Extras cover, depending on the product you choose.
What's the difference between physiotherapy and chiropractic treatment?
Physiotherapy focuses on movement, rehabilitation and recovery, while chiropractic treatment focuses on the diagnosis and management of musculoskeletal conditions, often involving spinal adjustments. Both can help with back, neck and joint pain, but they use different techniques and treatment approaches.
What's the difference between physiotherapy and exercise physiology?
Physiotherapy and exercise physiology are both allied health services, but they focus on different aspects of health and recovery.
A physiotherapist diagnoses and treats movement problems, pain and injuries using techniques such as manual therapy, rehabilitation exercises and physical treatments.
An exercise physiologist focuses on exercise-based treatment and lifestyle programs to help manage chronic health conditions, improve physical function and support long-term health goals.
Both practitioners may work together as part of a person's treatment and recovery plan.
At Australian Unity, most Extras products cover both physiotherapy and exercise physiology. These services are often combined under the same annual limit, giving you the flexibility to use your available benefits in a way that best suits your healthcare needs.
